posts.title: This meeting could have been a prompt
posts.description: A lot of the meetings on my calendar today seem to exist to gather something. Get everyone’s status so the group can align. Articulate two options side by side to compare. Create a report for the people who weren’t in the room. In each case, we (humans) are moving information from one place to another. Most of that can be a prompt right now. The context is already there: in docs, threads, and trac

posts.title: Please no more WhatsApp
posts.description: Someone drops a link in a chat: “I made a WhatsApp group for this, join here.” A school project, a street party, a daycare parents exchange, yet another neighbourhood initiative. Within a minute fifteen people are in, photos are flowing, and the thing basically organizes itself. I get it. WhatsApp is super easy. You install it once, it finds everyone you know, and it removes almost all the frictio

posts.title: A word search generator for a six-year-old who loves letters
posts.description: Our youngest is six and deep in the phase where letters are magic. She fills pages with experiments: her name, words she’s sounded out, invented spellings that are almost right and somehow more charming for it. Reading is clicking into place in real time and it’s one of those things you can’t quite believe you’re watching. We started doing word search puzzles together. She loves the hunt, scanning
